newsitem.title: Italy: SOCCER-ZANETTI PUTS INTER TOP AS JUVE AND MILAN DROP POINTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZANETTI PUTS INTER TOP AS JUVE AND MILAN DROP POINTS.

text.p: Argentine Javier Zanetti's late solo effort gave Inter a 1-0 win at Verona on Sunday and a one-point lead at the top of serie A as title rivals Milan and Juventus slipped to disappointing home draws.
Zanetti picked up the ball wide on the right with five minutes remaining and made a mazy run into the Verona penalty area before beating goalkeeper Attilio Gregori.

The last-gasp win took full advantage of Juventus's 1-1 draw at home to Napoli and Atalanta's courageous performance at the San Siro, where champions Milan needed a second-half penalty from Demetrio Albertini to salvage a point.
Inter, taken to a penalty shoot-out before eliminating Austria's Graz from the UEFA Cup last week, lead serie A with 17 points from eight matches, one ahead of Vicenza and two clear of Juve.
Vicenza have never gone better than runners-up in Serie A in 92 years but, until Zanetti's late goal for Inter, they briefly threatened to go top with their 2-0 win at Lazio
Playing against a side still reeling from a 5-3 UEFA Cup defeat at Tenerife, the visitors took the lead in the 35th minute through Roberto Murgita.

The home side, who scored an average of three goals a game at the Olympic stadium last season but who total four in four matches this year, then hit the woodwork three times before Giampiero Maini sealed three points with a late second.
Despite Lazio's perilous position -- fifth from bottom -- and elimination from Europe, club president Sergio Cragnotti gave manager Zdenek Zeman a vote of confidence.
Juventus coach Marcello Lippi blamed his side's indifferent performace at Turin on fatigue.

The European champions struggled to break down Napoli's defence in the first half, relying on a mistake from goalkeeper Giuseppe Taglialatela for Zinedine Zidane's opener in the 43rd minute -- the Frenchman's second goal in three league matches.
After the break a visibly tired Juve looked a pale shadow of the side which overwhelmed Austria's Rapid Vienna in the European Cup and Alfredo Aglietti claimed a deserved equaliser.
Roberto Mancini, the most prolific striker in serie A with 130 goals, celebrated his 400th and possibly last match for Sampdoria with two goals in a 3-0 home win over Piacenza.
If, as rumoured, Mancini is about to move to Inter, at least he is leaving Sampdoria high in the table -- level third with Milan and Bologna, 3-2 winners over Roma.
Gianluigi Lentini arrived at Milan in 1992 as the world's most expensive player but left this year never having fulfilled his potential after nearly losing his life in a car accident.
On Sunday Lentini reminded Milan of what they are missing by setting up Felippo Inzaghi's shock 21st-minute opener -- his seventh goal of the season -- with a mesmerising run.
One down at halftime, Milan coach Oscar Washington Tabarez brought on Christophe Dugarry and the Frenchman responded by winning the penalty from which Albertini struck the equaliser.
But Tabarez's second substitute, Roberto Baggio, failed to work the same magic, hitting the woodwork twice.
Down to 10 men after Inzaghi's late dismissal, Marco Sgro nearly stole all three points for Atalanta when his last-minute shot cannoned back of the post.
At Bologna, manager Renzo Ulivieri was dismissed from the bench for protesting but that did nothing to blunt his tactical acumen.

With Roma threatening a late comeback after Abel Balbo's 64th-minute penalty had made the score 2-1, Ulivieri, sitting in the stands, brought on striker Pierpaolo Bresciani. Within minutes Bresciani struck a crucial third goal.
